### How to read this page
Every loan application goes through five automated checks: **identity, documents, income, credit and policy**. The AI prepares a report and a **person always makes the final decision**. This page shows how many cases were handled, what the AI used, how fast it was, and whether anything needs attention.

**Colours:** 🟢 green = good  ·  🟠 amber = take a look  ·  🔴 red = a problem  ·  Hover the small **i** on any panel for a plain-language explanation. Totals count everything since the application was last started.

panels.title: 1. Cases: what came in and what was recommended
Cases finished
panels.description: How many applications the system has finished checking.

panels.title: Recommend approve
panels.description: Cases that scored high enough to recommend approval. A person still decides.

panels.title: Refer to officer
panels.description: Borderline cases that need a careful human look.

panels.title: Recommend reject
panels.description: Cases that scored low or broke a hard rule.

panels.title: Needs a fix
panels.description: Cases stopped because something can be corrected, such as a wrong or unreadable document.

panels.title: Officer decisions
panels.description: Times an officer confirmed or overrode the recommendation.

panels.title: Cases by recommendation
panels.description: Share of finished cases by what the system recommended.

panels.title: What officers did
panels.description: Confirm = officer agreed with the recommendation. Override = officer chose differently and wrote a reason.

panels.title: Cases finished over time
panels.description: Each bar is the number of cases finished in a short window.

panels.title: Total AI cost (USD)
panels.description: Money spent on AI calls. Free-tier models cost nothing.

panels.title: AI text processed
panels.description: Total size of what the AI read and wrote, counted in tokens (small pieces of words).

panels.title: Cost per case (USD)
panels.description: Average AI cost for one finished case.

panels.title: AI text per case
panels.description: Average tokens used for one finished case.

panels.title: Which step uses the most AI
panels.description: Total AI text used by each of the checking steps.

panels.title: AI usage over time
panels.description: How much AI text was used in each short window, by step.

panels.title: Average time per step
panels.description: How long one checking step takes on average. Under 10 seconds is green.

panels.title: Average AI reply time
panels.description: How long the AI takes to answer one request, on average.

panels.title: Time taken by each step
panels.description: Average seconds for each step. Longer bar = slower step.

panels.title: AI reply time by step
panels.description: Average seconds the AI took to answer, for each step.

panels.title: Backup AI used
panels.description: How many times the main AI was busy and a backup model answered instead. Occasional use is normal on free plans.

panels.title: Answers sent for checking
panels.description: Cases where an AI answer could not be double-checked and was passed to the officer marked 'unverified'. Zero is best.

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: Problems written to the application log. Zero is best.

panels.title: Backup AI use by step
panels.description: Which steps needed the backup model most.

panels.title: Unchecked answers by step
panels.description: Which steps produced answers that could not be verified.

panels.title: 5. Learning from officer overrides, and problem log
Precedent activity
panels.description: When an officer overrides, the system may save a 'precedent' that an admin must approve. Safety checks can hold unsafe ones back.

panels.title: Recent warnings and errors
panels.description: Only appears when something went wrong. Empty is good.
